summary: Invoice shows blended tariff after regional failover and hosted-fallback despite reserved dedicated pin
description:
Issue summary:
Customer EdgeLogix reports an unexpected blended (hosted+dedicated) tariff applied to the March 1-7 billing window after an automatic regional failover. They are on a dedicated contract with a pinned reserved capacity rate; invoice shows several line-items billed at hosted rates for requests routed to eu-west during the failover window.

Impact:
- Customer reports ~18% higher invoice than expected for the week (estimated $8.5k delta).
- Customer is an enterprise dedicated customer and needs an explanation + corrective action before month-end close.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: edge-001 (us-west) primary.
- Fallback routing policy: host-on-saturation (should fall back to dedicated-compatible hosted variant but not billed at hosted rate for reserved customers).
- Failover occurred 2026-03-03 02:13 UTC due to transient scheduler eviction in us-west.

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Normal requests from EdgeLogix routed to dedicated pool in us-west (pinned rate).
2) 2026-03-03 02:12 UTC: autoscaler eviction started on node GPU-12 in us-west causing transient capacity drop.
3) Smart routing policy triggered failover to eu-west for ~45 minutes while autoscaling recovered.
4) Customer observed traffic routed to eu-west; billing shows those requests were charged at hosted per-token rates instead of applying the reserved-dedicated reconciliation logic.

Logs & evidence attached:
- EdgeLogix provided invoice PDF (edge_invoice_Mar_week1.pdf) and sample request IDs: req-8a3f2, req-8a3f7.
- Support retrieved router logs and postback traces: router-trace-20260303-0215.log, postback-queue-20260303-logs.zip.
- Billing reconciler output snapshot for that window retained in S3: s3://billing-recon/2026-03-03/edge-001-snapshot.json.

Customer request:
- Clarify why hosted rates were applied to requests that should have been covered by reserved capacity and provide provisional credit if billing error confirmed.
comments: 2026-03-10 10:05 UTC - Asha Patel (Support): Opened with customer-provided invoice and request IDs; requested billing traces and permission to access their usage snapshots.

2026-03-10 13:42 UTC - Marco Ruiz (Billing eng): Pulled billing-recon snapshot; initial diff shows tickets routed to eu-west tagged 'fallback' and reconciler applied hosted rate mapping for 'fallback' events — investigating mapping logic for dedicated customers.
2026-03-11 09:18 UTC - EdgeLogix (Customer): Confirmed timeframe and provided additional request samples; asks for provisional credit while investigation continues.

2026-03-11 15:27 UTC - Marco Ruiz (Billing eng): Reproduced rate-mapping behavior in staging using a replay of the routing events; hypothesis: the reconciler treats 'fallback' flag as non-dedicated unless a dedicated-fallback tag is present on router-postback.

2026-03-12 08:04 UTC - Sophie Chen (SRE): Found that during the scheduler eviction the postback writer dropped 'pool_id' on ~3100 requests due to a buffer overflow; without pool_id reconciler falls back to hosted rate path.
2026-03-12 11:30 UTC - Marco Ruiz (Billing eng): Proposed remediation path and provisional credit for the delta; awaiting finance sign-off for credit issuance.
2026-03-12 16:05 UTC - Asha Patel (Support): Notified customer we are working on provisional credit and will follow up with final invoice adjustment and root cause postmortem.
investigation_notes: Reconciler behavior: current logic applies dedicated rate only when 'pool_id' or 'reserved_tag' present in postback. 'fallback' flag alone routes to hosted price table.
Postback loss: SRE confirmed buffer overflow in postback-writer during ~02:12-02:58 UTC which caused loss of pool_id for subset of events (3100 events).
Staging replay: replayed routing events with missing pool_id yields same hosted-rate mapping — confirms mapping gap.
Frequency: affected events represent ~7% of EdgeLogix's weekly requests and align with the invoice delta reported by customer.

Immediate mitigation: patch postback-writer to retry on buffer full errors and add defensive tagging to include 'pool_id' before enqueueing. Patch candidate: PR #214 (billing-reconciler) references changes to accept 'fallback_with_reserved' tag.
Longer-term: update reconciler mapping to consult routing metadata service (route-metadata) when pool_id missing to infer dedicated coverage; add automated test for postback drop scenarios.
resolution: Provisional credit approved for the estimated $8.5k delta; Finance issued a provisional credit on 2026-03-12 (memo EDGE-CR-20260312). Engineering deployed an emergency patch to postback-writer (rollback safe) to add retry-on-buffer-full and defensive pool_id enrichment (deployed 2026-03-12 12:45 UTC). Billing reconciler PR #214 merged to accept 'fallback_with_reserved' tag and reconciled the March 1-7 window; final invoice adjustment scheduled for next billing cycle. Follow-ups: (1) postmortem to be created in Confluence and shared with customer, (2) reconciler to consult route-metadata service for missing pool_id cases, (3) add end-to-end e2e test for failover billing. Customer notified and satisfied with provisional credit; close after final invoice updated.
